A change in the cultural atmosphere can change the very expectations that one attaches with a certain concept, and love is no exception to this belief. I moved from Calcutta to Delhi to Varanasi, and in all the three cities, I found a different concept of what one would call love. Love is neither a universal constant nor is it independent of any variables concerning it. It does strongly vary as the conditions around the potential lovers change. At this position, it is possible that my understanding of all of these is very empirical, rather than a rational abstraction or conceptualisation. When in Calcutta, love meant companionship amalgamated with great comfort; a lover was usually one’s best friend, a mushy blanket that one could ever ask for. In Delhi, love became more outright as well as more commodified; people often confused love with physical attraction, everyone had everyone else as a possible partner and it was all too chaotic. Love in Varanasi became quite synonymous with life itself, reviving the very initial showers of this emotion; love here was slow, platonic and contentful; love in this city was a respite!
